# MLX-LM training memory and gradient control — facts

> Source-anchored units about MLX-LM training memory and gradient control: 9 across 5 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## Structure and components

- [statement] MLX-LM's guide also recommends reducing `--batch-size`, `--num-layers`, or example length to lower memory; it cautions that training fewer layers may reduce quality on data-heavy runs, while research treats microbatching and checkpointing as separate techniques with workload-dependent memory and compute tradeoffs. (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/0d4d3d04f8ab7ce4a51e7209e8615755a48ba94d/mlx_lm/LORA.md · keywords: MLX-LM training memory and gradient control · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.10631
- [statement] --grad-checkpoint enables training gradient checkpointing. --batch-size reduces examples in each minibatch, while --num-layers reduces the last-layer subset selected for training. For one worker, batch_size B and --grad-accumulation-steps A combine A minibatches before an optimizer update, giving an effective example batch size B*A. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/0d4d3d04f8ab7ce4a51e7209e8615755a48ba94d/mlx_lm/lora.py · keywords: MLX-LM training memory and gradient control · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/0d4d3d04f8ab7ce4a51e7209e8615755a48ba94d/mlx_lm/tuner/trainer.py

## How it works

- [statement] train() rejects grad_accumulation_steps below one with ValueError("grad_accumulation_steps must be at least 1"). It sums successive microbatch gradients; at an update it calls average_gradients, divides each accumulated gradient by grad_accumulation_steps when greater than one, then calls optimizer.update. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/0d4d3d04f8ab7ce4a51e7209e8615755a48ba94d/mlx_lm/tuner/trainer.py · keywords: MLX-LM training memory and gradient control

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A June 2025 user report recorded Metal `Insufficient Memory` at a reported 34.108 GB peak with batch size 1, `--grad-checkpoint`, and a 5,000-token maximum sequence; after reinstalling MLX-LM from source, the follow-up log reached iteration 100, so the report does not isolate a memory-control limit or give a portable capacity estimate. (low confidence) — https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/issues/236 · keywords: MLX-LM training memory and gradient control
- [statement] Activation memory grows with batch size and sequence length, so the MLX-LM guide recommends lowering `--batch-size` and shortening long examples when memory is constrained; it notes that smaller batches may slow training. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/blob/main/mlx_lm/LORA.md · keywords: MLX-LM training memory and gradient control · also: https://pytorch.org/blog/activation-checkpointing-techniques/
- [statement] iterate_batches truncates examples longer than max_seq_length, emits a warning, and updates the recorded lengths to the truncated lengths. If the dataset contains fewer examples than batch_size, it raises ValueError stating that the dataset must have at least batch_size examples. Pre-split long examples and choose a batch size no larger than the dataset. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/0d4d3d04f8ab7ce4a51e7209e8615755a48ba94d/mlx_lm/tuner/trainer.py · keywords: MLX-LM training memory and gradient control

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] MLX-LM's `--grad-checkpoint` trades extra computation for lower activation memory by recomputing intermediate values needed during backpropagation; its guide says the option is more helpful with larger batches or sequences. Framework documentation describes the same recomputation tradeoff and notes that checkpoint placement affects peak-memory savings. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/blob/main/mlx_lm/LORA.md · keywords: MLX-LM training memory and gradient control · also: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/v5.10.1/en/grad_checkpointing, https://pytorch.org/blog/activation-checkpointing-techniques/, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/0d4d3d04f8ab7ce4a51e7209e8615755a48ba94d/mlx_lm/LORA.md, https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.10631
- [statement] As of 2026-10-23, open MLX-LM issue #1206 contains reports of Qwen3.5 training OOM despite `--grad-checkpoint` on M5 Max and M3 Pro systems, alongside a base-M5 report that the OOM was not reproducible and training completed normally through iteration 5; treat this as configuration-specific evidence rather than a general memory limit. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/issues/1206 · keywords: MLX-LM training memory and gradient control

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MLX-LM's memory guide says `--grad-accumulation-steps N` accumulates gradients across N batches before updating, so users can keep each microbatch small while increasing effective batch size without increasing batch memory; Hugging Face's training documentation describes the same effective-batch relationship. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/0d4d3d04f8ab7ce4a51e7209e8615755a48ba94d/mlx_lm/LORA.md · keywords: MLX-LM training memory and gradient control · also: https://huggingface.co/docs/accelerate/usage_guides/gradient_accumulation, https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/blob/main/mlx_lm/LORA.md, https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.10631
